title: Trade usage and the commercial setting
shortTitle: Trade usage and the commercial setting
summary: A trade usage is a sufficiently established practice in a business that helps determine what parties in that setting reasonably understand their agreement to mean or require.
notes:
Frigaliment asks what “chicken” meant in the relevant transaction and who had proved the narrower meaning. Hurst asks whether a numerical protein specification carried an established trade tolerance. Nanakuli examines price protection as a practice relevant to an asphalt supply agreement. Bayway uses industry evidence to assess whether an added tax term would objectively surprise a merchant.

Identify the practice precisely, establish the evidence supporting it, and explain its relationship to the disputed term. Trade usage is different from a course of dealing between these particular parties and from a course of performance under this very agreement. The readings show that practice may explain, supplement, or qualify language in some circumstances; it is not a license to disregard every express term.
